title: Scaling Socratic Statistics Instruction Through Large Language Models
content: Socratic teaching promotes statistical reasoning through questioning, dialogue, and guided inquiry, but its implementation is difficult to scale because it requires skilled instructors and sustained learner interaction. This study examined whether large language models can support scalable Socratic statistics instruction. A Socratic Learning Analysis Scheme was developed by adapting the Cambridge Dialogue Analysis Scheme to assess key features of Socratic learning: inquiry, knowledge construction, dialectical examination, reflective transfer, and learning progression. Forty simulated tutoring dialogues were generated between an AI Socratic instructor and a novice undergraduate student and evaluated by an expert educator. An overall Socratic Learning Index (SLI) was calculated for each dialogue. The mean SLI was 81.1%, with 65% of dialogues classified as Highly Socratic Learning. Strong performance was observed in inquiry, reasoning, and dialectical examination. These findings provide preliminary evidence that LLMs can generate dialogue aligned with Socratic pedagogy and may help scale inquiry-based statistics education.
